Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is the classic radiographic presentation of a massive right pleural effusion exerting mass effect. A tension pneumothorax would appear hyperlucent rather than opaque, and consolidation or atelectasis would typically cause an ipsilateral shift or no significant shift.
